subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up - PayWise discovery
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@paywise.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up - PayWise discovery

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can get the right technical resources looped in.

Summary of what you shared:
- Data types: payment PAN (tokenized on your side), customer PII (name, email, phone), payment metadata, support transcripts.
- Data residency: production data must remain in US-East region (us-east-1).
- Retention: transactional/payment records = 7 years; customer support transcripts = 13 months.
- Logging: You want access to request-level logs for troubleshooting but need controls to prevent PII leakage (filtered/hashed fields and role-based access).
- Encryption: Strong preference for customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backend; at-rest encryption required; in-transit TLS 1.2+ accepted.

Ask / next steps we discussed:
1) Can you confirm the primary technical contact for KMS integration (SRE or security engineer) so we can schedule a 30–45 min deep dive?
2) Any mandatory compliance artifacts we should prepare up front (SOC 2, encryption key policies, key rotation SLAs)?
3) Confirm whether key escrow or third-party HSM (Custodial vs. Customer-managed HSM) is required.

Attaching a short overview of our KMS options and BYOK workflow: redwood-kms-overview.pdf. I’ll follow up internally to capture which artifacts we can share immediately (SOC 2, key rotation policy, architecture diagram).

If the above looks right, I’ll propose a couple of times for the technical deep-dive next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-kms-overview.pdf

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@paywise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris Lee <chris.lee@paywise.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS follow-up - PayWise discovery

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That's accurate. A few clarifications from our side:
- We do require customer-managed keys (BYOK) and they must be HSM-backed (FIPS 140-2 level 3 or equivalent).
- Data residency: yes, all production data and keys must remain in the US (prefer us-east-1).
- Retention: confirmed — payment records 7 years, transcripts 13 months.
- Logging: we need request-level metadata for debug but with PII redaction. Retention for logs should be 13 months as well.

Technical contacts: looping in Chris Lee (SRE) — he will take ownership of the KMS deep-dive and review the architecture.

Could you also provide:
- SOC 2 type II report (or SOC 2 attestation) and any high-level KMS/key rotation policy docs?
- A short runbook describing how Redwood supports BYOK (key import, rotation, revocation, and emergency access).

Timing: we’re targeting an internal security review next Thursday (29 Apr). If you can get the artifacts before then and book a tech call this week, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Director of Security & Compliance | PayWise
Samantha.Ortiz@paywise.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Encryption & KMS follow-up - PayWise discovery

Folks —

Samantha confirmed BYOK with HSM and the retention/residency constraints. Chris (SRE) is the technical owner. They also asked for SOC 2 and a BYOK runbook before their internal review next Thu (29 Apr).

Immediate items I recommend we prepare this week:
- Pull SOC 2 Type II attestation and the redacted controls matrix (I’ve flagged SOC artifacts in the shared drive).
- Produce a 1–2 page BYOK runbook that covers: key import process, rotation (recommended cadence), revocation, emergency procedures, and how we handle backups/escrow.
- Validate supported HSM providers and options we can offer: AWS KMS (BYOK import), AWS CloudHSM (dedicated HSM), and a managed HSM partner (bring-your-own HSM via partner).
- Create a short KMS options matrix (kms-options-matrix.xlsx) comparing trade-offs (latency, operator burden, cost, compliance posture).

Questions for infra/security:
- Can we guarantee keys stay in us-east-1 for PayWise (no geo-replication)?
- What are the SLAs around key rotation and re-encryption windows for customer-managed keys?

I attached SOC artifacts we can share (soc2-evidence.zip) and the blank KMS options doc I’ll start filling out. I’ll draft the BYOK runbook and share for review.

Marissa

Attachments: soc2-evidence.zip; kms-options-matrix.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@paywise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Chris Lee <chris.lee@paywise.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS follow-up - PayWise discovery

Hi Samantha & Chris —

Thanks for the clear requirements and for looping Chris in. Next steps from our side:
1) We will send the SOC 2 Type II cover letter and a redacted controls summary by end of day today (attached in the drive).
2) Draft BYOK runbook (1–2 page) + KMS options matrix — target to share by EOD Fri (23 Apr).
3) Schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive the week of 26 Apr. Please share 2–3 time windows that work for you; we’ll propose matching slots for our infra/security engineers.

Notes on the key questions you raised:
- Keys and production data: we can provision customer-managed keys scoped to a single region (us-east-1) and do not enable automatic geo-replication unless explicitly requested.
- HSM-backed requirement: we support BYOK via AWS KMS import for customer-managed keys and can offer CloudHSM-backed keys for stricter FIPS 140-2 Level 3 requirements. We will include a short comparison in the matrix.
- Key rotation & re-encryption: rotation schedule is configurable; recommended default is 90 days for rotation of wrapping keys with a documented re-encryption window. We’ll include expected timelines and operational impact in the runbook.

Sharing a drive folder with artifacts and the proposed runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-paywise-enc-kms

If that plan works, we’ll book the deep-dive after we get your available times.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
